critical_code_review_comments: services/northena/interfaces.py line 24: `RegistryHandle = object` is a plain alias, not a Protocol. Adequate for the N-INV-11 boundary (opaque pass-through) and correctly documented in the docstring, but if future stages want structural typing on the registry, promote to `Protocol` in a later phase.

services/northena/admit.py line 54: `registry: Optional[RegistryStub] = None` — the composer (state_machine) now passes an `Optional[RegistryHandle]` (object) into a param typed as `Optional[RegistryStub]`. Runtime is fine (Python duck-typed, admit.py falls back to `RegistryStub()` when None). Static-type-checker (mypy/pyright) would flag if strictness were increased, but at G2a this is acceptable and preserves the mandate §13.11 boundary (only admit.py names the concrete Solva type).

N-INV-11 test uses substring greps ('from services.solva' / 'import services.solva'). interfaces.py mentions 'services.solva_depth' inside a comment but does NOT contain the two forbidden literals, so the test correctly passes. The comment is the intended documentation of the boundary and should be preserved.

rca of the issue.root_cause: services/northena/state_machine.py previously imported RegistryStub directly from services.solva_depth.admit_assist to type its optional pass-through param, which violated mandate §13 invariant #11 (governors orthogonal — Solva imports permitted ONLY inside admit.py).
rca of the issue.fix_applied_by_main_agent: 1) Added `RegistryHandle = object` opaque alias to services/northena/interfaces.py with a boundary-explaining comment. 2) Changed state_machine.py to `from services.northena.interfaces import RegistryHandle` and re-typed the pass-through param as `Optional[RegistryHandle] = None`.
